findings.claim: User.locations is the only @ManyToMany collection on a core domain class with no addX/removeX mutators, and it follows neither of the two shapes its siblings use to guarantee non-nullness, so the field Javadoc's 'an empty set means the user is unrestricted' contract is not actually enforced.
findings.evidence: Enumerated every @ManyToMany in the domain package at b7cd909: `git grep -n '@ManyToMany' -- 'api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/*.java'` gives exactly 5 - ConceptName.java:100, Location.java:145, OrderType.java:64, User.java:95 (roles), User.java:108 (locations, new). All four pre-existing ones carry mutators: User.addRole/removeRole (User.java:343, 361, both null-tolerant), Location.addTag/removeTag (Location.java:582, 597), ConceptName.addTag/removeTag (ConceptName.java:406, 424), OrderType.addConceptClass (OrderType.java:196). The closest structural sibling is OrderType.conceptClasses - also @Independent + @ManyToMany + @JoinTable with no cascade - and it does BOTH: lazy-initialises inside the getter (OrderType.java:159-163, `if (conceptClasses == null) conceptClasses = new LinkedHashSet<>();`) and exposes addConceptClass. The lazy-init-getter shape is also what Person.getNames (Person.java:406-411) and Concept.getNames (Concept.java:1040-1042) use. The new field instead initialises inline and exposes only get/set: User.java:372-374 returns the field, User.java:379-381 assigns the argument, so setLocations(null) puts the field back to null - which is exactly why UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations still has to defend with `assigned == null` (UserServiceImpl.java:866-869) despite the Javadoc promise. Concrete cost visible in this PR: LocationServiceTest.java:554 has to write `user.setLocations(new HashSet<>(Collections.singletonList(locationToDelete)))` for want of an addLocation, and the companion REST subresource described in the PR body (POST/DELETE one location at a time) will repeat that copy-mutate-set on every call.

findings.claim: Splicing the LOCATION_ID constant into the SQL text to name a bind parameter (":" + LOCATION_ID) has no precedent in api/src/main/java, and it converted a previously greppable query string at line 477 into a concatenation.
findings.evidence: `git grep -n ':" + [A-Z_]' -- 'api/src/main/java'` returns only HibernateLocationDAO.java:133 and :477, both written or edited by this PR (positive control for the pipeline: the same pattern search over the tree also surfaces the unrelated PatientServiceImpl.java:1521 and OpenmrsConstants.java:785, so it is not a silently-empty grep). The established shape for exactly this constant idiom is HibernateObsDAO: `private static final String OBS_ID = "obsId"` (line 62) is used only as a JPA attribute path / sort field (lines 211, 214, 376), while the native query at HibernateObsDAO.java:526 keeps `:obsId` literal inside the SQL string. Extracting the constant for setParameter (which is what the SonarCloud duplicate-literal finding actually needed) matches that precedent; splicing it into the query text does not, and it means `parent_location = :locationId` and `location_id = :locationId` can no longer be found by searching the query as written.

findings.claim: The comment directly above the constant this PR bumps names the wrong trigger - it says the constant needs updating 'when adding new Liquibase update files', when in fact any new changeset in an existing update file requires it, as this PR demonstrates.
findings.evidence: Read DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT.java:28-37 at b7cd909: the comment is 'This constant needs to be updated when adding new Liquibase update files to openmrs-core.' and the constant covers 'the Liquibase snapshot files 2.1.x and all Liquibase update files with versions greater than 2.1.x'. This PR added no new file - the changeset went into the existing api/src/main/resources/org/openmrs/liquibase/updates/liquibase-update-to-latest-3.0.x.xml (which already held 13 changesets) - yet the constant still had to move 916 -> 917, and per the PR body that mismatch is what failed the -Pintegration-test job. The PR body itself paraphrases the comment as 'whenever a new changeset is added', i.e. as what it should have said. Worth correcting while the line is being touched. (History check was not available: the clone is shallow, .git/shallow present, 416 commits, and `git log -S CHANGE_SET_COUNT_FOR_GREATER_THAN_2_1_X` returns only one unrelated boundary commit, so I could not confirm how earlier changeset-only additions handled this.)

findings.claim: The DML statement goes through createNativeQuery(...).executeUpdate() on a raw NativeQuery, where the only other native DELETE in this package uses Hibernate's createNativeMutationQuery.
findings.evidence: `javap -cp ~/.m2/repository/org/hibernate/orm/hibernate-core/7.4.7.Final/hibernate-core-7.4.7.Final.jar -p org.hibernate.query.QueryProducer` (7.4.7.Final is the version bom/pom.xml:53 pins) shows `createNativeQuery(String)` returning a raw, un-parameterised org.hibernate.query.NativeQuery alongside `createNativeMutationQuery(String)` returning MutationQuery. The nearest in-package sibling for the same job - a native DELETE against a table that is not a mapped entity - is HibernateConceptDAO.deleteSubclassConcept (HibernateConceptDAO.java:265-270), which uses createNativeMutationQuery; HibernateConceptDAO.java:203 does the same for an INSERT. This stays a nit rather than a suggestion because there is a counter-instance in the same file: HibernateConceptDAO.java:238 uses createNativeQuery for an INSERT, so the project is not uniform. Nothing would flag the raw type either - maven-compiler-plugin is configured with encoding only, no -Xlint (pom.xml:111-116).

what_i_swept: Two passes at b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2 against merge base 28e3bab (diffstat verified: 8 files, +216/-6). Pass 1 walked each changed file top to bottom and compared it against its nearest in-tree sibling: the Liquibase changeset against every hand-written createTable changeset in api/src/main/resources/org/openmrs/liquibase/updates/ (2.5.x-3.0.x) and against the generated user_role/location_tag_map definitions in the 1.9.x and 2.9.x schema snapshots (id format, author style, preConditions/comment order, standalone addPrimaryKey, absence of a uuid column on a pure join table, FK naming, and the deferrable/initiallyDeferred/onDelete attribute set plus its wrapped-attribute layout); User.locations against all five @ManyToMany mappings in org.openmrs and against @Independent's own Javadoc and its two other usages; the UserService/UserServiceImpl additions against the file's own @Authorized / @Transactional(readOnly=true) / Context.get*Service() / PrivilegeConstants / @since / Should-before-@param patterns, plus a 1:1 check that each of the five Should lines has a matching test method name; the two tests against their immediate neighbours (LocationServiceTest.purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationSuccessfully, and the javadoc-free recent tests at the tail of UserServiceTest), including whether the imports they need were already present; and the DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT bump against the constant's own documentation. I also established what CI actually enforces before flagging anything stylistic: spotless (OpenMRSFormatter.xml, importOrder java|javax,jakarta,org,com,,\#) runs in the build, while checkstyle.xml exists but the plugin appears only in and in no or block, and the workflows run plain `mvn clean install` + `mvn test` - so I measured the added line lengths and import ordering, found the 139-char @JoinTable line is preceded by an already-128-char user_role line, and dropped those. Pass 2 traced one level out: envers (is a user_location audit table conventionally created in liquibase? no - hibernate.integration.envers.enabled=false, suffix is _audit, and _audit appears nowhere under api/src/main/resources but hibernate.default.properties); the generated schema/core-data snapshots (author="rafal (generated)", none past 2.9.x, so a feature PR leaves them alone); hibernate.cfg.xml and the .hbm.xml set (User and Location are annotation-mapped and unlisted, nothing to register); messages.properties (checked whether recent field additions - Drug.description, Provider.description, Privilege.name, ConceptReferenceRange, ProviderRole - added keys: none did, convention dead); UserValidator and the web module (no field enumeration that a new collection would need to join); CreateInitialDataSet.java's hardcoded table list (dead - lists nothing added since ~1.x); the inverse-side join-table sibling HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocationTag and LocationServiceImpl.purgeLocation/purgeLocationTag; and the naming vocabulary (AdministrationService.getAllowedLocales is a direct precedent for getAllowedLocations, OrderService returns List five times so a cross-domain return type from UserService is precedented too). Pass 2 is what turned up conventions-1's strongest evidence (OrderType.conceptClasses), so it was not a wasted pass; the third sweep over the remaining surface produced only items already killed by prior instances.
out_of_scope: Authorization: the new method authorises on PrivilegeConstants.GET_LOCATIONS, the first non-user privilege on any UserService method (13 GET_USERS, 5 EDIT_USER_PASSWORDS, etc.) - whether a user needs GET_LOCATIONS to resolve their own login locations is the security reviewer's call.

Performance: getAllowedLocations loads every location carrying the tag via Context.getLocationService().getLocationsByTag(tag) and intersects in Java (UserServiceImpl.java:865-871) instead of pushing the join to a DAO query, and it re-reads the User by id on every call.
Correctness: Set.contains on Hibernate entities in the intersection relies on BaseOpenmrsObject equality; and getLocationsByTag has no includeRetired flag, so retired tagged locations may come back.
Correctness: the native DELETE in deleteLocation bypasses the session cache (the author documents this in a comment), and setLocations replaces a managed PersistentSet wholesale.

Test coverage: three of the five new UserServiceTest assertions check only hasSize, never which locations came back; no test asserts that the FK purge fix fails on the base commit; nothing covers a retired assigned location.

Solution fit: TRUNK-6669 specifies a user_location_id surrogate PK, leaf-locations-only semantics, and POST/DELETE endpoints; this PR ships a composite PK and no REST surface (deferred to webservices.rest#762), and names the method getAllowedLocations rather than the ticket's getLoginLocationsForUser.
could_not_verify: The clone is shallow (.git/shallow present, 416 commits reachable), so no convention claim here could be checked against commit history - `git log -S CHANGE_SET_COUNT_FOR_GREATER_THAN_2_1_X` returns a single unrelated boundary commit rather than the constant's real history. Every finding rests on the state of the tree at b7cd909 instead.

I ran no Maven build (mvn install is banned on this shared ~/.m2 and builds are contended), so nothing here is backed by a test run. No finding needed one: conventions-1's setLocations(null) behaviour is read off the two-line accessor pair at User.java:372-381 rather than executed, and I have flagged that rather than dressing a source read up as a runtime confirmation.

Whether checkstyle runs anywhere outside this repo's pom (e.g. in a Bamboo or SonarCloud step I cannot see) - I found it only in <pluginManagement>, so I treated its rules as advisory and dropped the LineLength and SummaryJavadoc observations.
